name: Template Method
intent: Define the skeleton of an algorithm in a base class and let subclasses fill in specific steps without changing the overall order.
scenario: Tea and coffee are prepared with the same recipe shape: boil water, brew, pour, optionally add extras. Only brewing and the extras differ.
problem: Tea and Coffee each have their own prepare() with the same steps copy-pasted. When the common steps change, you must fix every copy, and the order can drift between them.
solution: Put the recipe in a base class method, prepare(), that calls the steps in a fixed order. Common steps are implemented once in the base. Different steps are abstract and subclasses override them. Optional steps are hooks with a default.
pain: Tea and Coffee both copy the same prepare() steps
A change to a shared step must be repeated in every class
The order of steps can drift between copies
A new drink means copying the whole recipe again
benefits: The recipe order lives in exactly one method
A new drink overrides only brew() and addCondiments()
Hooks let subclasses opt in or out of optional steps
whenToUse: Several classes share the same algorithm shape and differ in a few steps
You want to control exactly which parts of an algorithm can be customised
Frameworks that call your code at fixed points: test setUp/tearDown, request handlers
whenNotToUse: The algorithms differ so much that the skeleton barely matches: use Strategy
You prefer composition to inheritance, or the language lacks good support for subclassing
pitfalls: Inheritance-based: subclasses are tied to the base class
Too many abstract steps make subclasses tedious to write
Violating the skeleton: subclasses that override the template method itself
Hard to follow control flow that jumps between base and subclass

roles.label: Abstract Class
roles.description: Owns the template method and the shared steps.

quiz.question: A CSV importer and a JSON importer each have a copy of: open file, validate, parse, save, close. Someone fixes the order in the CSV one, but the JSON one still saves before validating. What design prevents this drift?
options: A shared utility class with open() and close() that both importers call in their own order
A base class with a fixed-order import() and a parse() hook
A code review rule that both importers must be changed together, each time
An interface Importer with the five methods, implemented separately by each class
quiz.explanation: Putting the order in one method in a base class means it exists once, and subclasses can only fill in parse(). Helpers and interfaces still let each class choose its own order. A review rule depends on people remembering.

quiz.question: A base class Exporter defines export() as: load, transform, write, with transform left for subclasses. A developer overrides export() itself in a subclass to skip the load step. What best protects the intended order?
options: Make transform() private in the base class so subclasses cannot see it
Make the base class concrete, so it can be tested without a subclass
Add a comment above export() asking subclasses not to override it
Mark export() as final, sealed or non-virtual, and expose only the steps for overriding
quiz.explanation: The skeleton is the point of the pattern, so the template method itself should not be overridable, where the language allows it. Hiding transform() would stop subclasses from supplying it at all. A comment or a concrete base is not enforced.

quiz.question: An Exporter must change format per request, from a user setting, and its class already extends a framework base class. The two formats share the same four steps and differ in two. A colleague proposes Template Method. What is the strongest objection?
options: Template Method requires every step to be abstract, and this skeleton has two shared steps
The format varies per request and the single base class is used, so composition fits better
Template Method is only meant for skeletons with three steps or fewer, and this one has four
Subclassing cannot share the common steps between two formats, so the shared code is duplicated
quiz.explanation: Template Method fixes the variation at class level through inheritance, and here the format is chosen per request on a class that cannot also extend another base. Composition with a swappable format object solves both. Subclasses can share the common steps, which is the pattern's strength.
